correctness.rationale: For finite a≥3, b≥1 and c=a−2, use the ordered active basis (e₋,e₊,e_B,e_C), with consecutive entries iγ, √(2b), η√(bc). The passive-A and B zero-sum complements are annihilated and contribute (c−1)+(b−1) dark modes. The tridiagonal determinant recurrence gives p₂=z²+γ², p₃=z(z²+γ²−2b), and p₄=zp₃−bcη²p₂=z⁴−A₀z²−C₀. For positive γ and η the two z² roots are real, opposite in sign and nonzero. The four simple active roots and the exact zero direct summand justify diagonalization, with growth exponent μ from the +iμ mode and a matching upper bound from the eigenbasis. At η=0 the trimer is a direct summand in the aggregate basis (not literally three graph vertices when b>1). Below threshold it has distinct real eigenvalues; at equality H³=0 but H² has a nonzero end-to-end entry, so the exponential has a nonzero t² term; above threshold its imaginary pair gives the asserted rate. For x=μ², use x²+A₀x−C₀=0. Below threshold x has leading order γ²bcη²/(2b−γ²) with O(η⁴) error; at equality x/η tends to √(2b²c) with O(η) error. Under γ²=2b+κη the positive root for x/η tends to (√(κ²+8b²c)+κ)/2. These checks independently reconstruct RESULT.md lines 44–72. The supplied verifier and requirements were inspected without running the uploaded script.

value.rationale: The calculation resolves a motivated stability question for an arbitrarily weak added passive channel. It gives the actual positive growth rate at fixed graph size and distinguishes its linear onset below the isolated EP3 from square-root onset at the critical gain, including the gain detuning scale on which the two regimes meet. This is a useful exact benchmark for interpreting stability near the trimer transition; no value is assigned to relabeling the same active star, counting spectators in isolation, or rederiving the trimer threshold alone.
